adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from a single object to an array and updates Google Calendar to select the calendar by matching `credentialId` (`calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`). In contrast, Lark and Office365 services still destructure only the first element (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []; const calendarId = mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId;`) for create/update/delete (Lark) and create (Office365). Meanwhile, `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` now iterates over every `destination` in `event.destinationCalendar` and calls `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each host/credential, implying multiple calendar events should be created. Because Lark/Office365 always use the first destination calendar, every host’s call would target the same calendar (the first element), and Lark can throw `"no calendar id"` even when the current credential’s destination calendar exists later in the array. This is a correctness regression for collective bookings with multiple destination calendars.
